item.title: Spanish Subtitles For This Clip

turns.text: Add Spanish subtitles to this English clip, please. Leave her voice in English and keep the whole video as it is.

item.tests: Tests faithful Spanish subtitle translation and timing while retaining the source English audio and footage.

answer_sheet.Target language and regional preference: Spanish; neutral, broadly understandable Spanish is fine.
answer_sheet.Translation wording: Your call; faithfully translate her greeting and offer to show three easy ways to make mornings less stressful.
answer_sheet.Subtitle delivery and style: Put readable Spanish subtitles on the video. Styling is your call.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: Preserve the source framing; free-tier 480p is fine.
answer_sheet.Audio: Keep her English voice unchanged. Do not dub or add music.

must_haves: The output retains the complete original 10-second kitchen-table footage.
Visible Spanish subtitles convey the greeting, 'today,' three easy ways, and making mornings less stressful.
The translation is natural Spanish and does not add advice that she never gives.
Spanish subtitle chunks follow the corresponding English speech and remain legible within the frame.
The original English speech remains audible, with no Spanish dub.

turns.text: Could you add Spanish subtitles to this English clip I've attached, please? I want to share it with people I know who are more comfortable reading Spanish. Her voice should stay in English, so please leave her voice unchanged. I get a little nervous that asking for subtitles will somehow turn into a bigger edit than I meant. Apart from adding the subtitles, please keep the whole video exactly as it is.

dialog.agent:
Your request is clear: **Spanish subtitles only**, with her English voice and everything else left unchanged.

Unfortunately, the connected subtitle tool doesn’t offer a translation-language setting, so I can’t reliably produce Spanish subtitles from this English clip here. I haven’t changed your video or started a generation.

If you provide the English transcript, I can translate it into Spanish for subtitles. If you have a timed subtitle file (SRT), I can translate it while preserving the timestamps, so it can accompany the original video without altering its audio or visuals.
dialog.why: It says the connected subtitle tool lacks a translation-language setting, so it cannot reliably produce the requested Spanish subtitles. It offers alternatives but does not deliver a result or ask a direct question.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

dialog.agent:
I understand—but this isn’t a free-plan limit: the subtitle tool has no option to translate English speech into Spanish. Trying it would likely add **English captions**, not Spanish ones.

Would you like English captions as a fallback? I won’t use voice translation or a generative video edit, since those would change parts you asked me to preserve.
dialog.why: It asks the user whether they want English captions as a fallback and waits for their choice.
dialog.user: Yes, go ahead with English captions as a fallback, though Spanish subtitles were what I was hoping for. Please use all 10 seconds of talk-one.mp4 and keep her English voice unchanged. Free-tier 480p is fine, and I’m still a little worried about this turning into a bigger edit than just adding captions.

turns.agent:
The captioning request was refused because your account doesn’t have enough credits. **No captioned video was created, and your original clip and English voice were not changed.**

Once credits are available, we can retry English captions for the full 10 seconds without requesting any other edits.
